messages:
alex_m: Heads-up — saw a big perf spike after today's runtime merge (runtimes/compile: autotune refactor). 2-3x tail latency on small-batch text-gen.
ci-bot: perf/benchmark runtime/p95 linux-gpu-16 -> +220% (suite: smoke-textgen)
jamal: repro steps? logs? can you paste a kernel decision dump?
alex_m: gist of dump:
```
autotune: selected kernel=matmul_v2, shape=[1,2048,1], cost=1200
expected_best=matmul_v1 cost=300
pick_reason=heuristic_score(0.98) from table v2
```
leah: ugh, that looks like the new heuristic scoring bumped v2 aggressively for small batches. could be due to the learning-rate scale change in the refactor
tara: also seeing compile storm in staging: 500 compiles queued, GPU utilization tanked while kernels compiled on demand. cache invalidations on every restart.
ops-bot: ALERT — compile-queue length 512 -> autoscale triggered
jamal: I started a git bisect locally. suspect commit 9b4d56a reversed the table key normalization. bisect points at 9b4d56a
alex_m: confirmed locally: when I force `autotune.table.normalize_keys=false` the pick goes back to matmul_v1 and perf is normal
leah: can we hotfix by pinning the autotune lookup to old-key behavior? quick patch: `lookup_key = legacy_key(shape, dtype)` in runtime path
tara: CI failing on perf gate: `perf-check` blocked rollout. We're blocked until revert/hotfix.
jamal: creating draft PR to pin behavior and add test to prevent key-shift. also adding cache-miss telemetry for future.
ci-bot: created task perf/regress/1768501234 - please link PR
alex_m: good. after PR we should run a targeted perf job (small-batch, seq_len=256, batch=1) and monitor compile-queue. If green, roll forward. :thumbsup:
leah: note — also add recording of compile artifacts so we don't recompile across minor restarts
tara: thanks all. I'll coordinate rollout freeze with release manager and mark this as rollout blocker
alex_m: ETA for PR review? jamal?
jamal: I have a draft, pushing patch now. cc @leah @tara
ops-bot: scheduled update: revert candidate queued on canary cluster
alex_m: great work. keep threads here; will follow up when canary perf is stable.
